# Comparator setup

* `comparator.json` names the compared theorems: `theorem_5_1`, `theorem_5_1_tendsto`,
  `theorem_5_1_unique` (Theorem 5.1), `theorem_5_2`, `theorem_5_2_deterministic`
  (Theorem 5.2) and `proposition_5_3` (Proposition 5.3), all in namespace `WeakPathwiseIto`.
* `WeakPathwiseItoComparator/Challenge.lean` is generated by `scripts/gen_challenge.py`:
  the import closure of `Main.Theorem51`, `Main.Theorem52`, `Main.Proposition53` flattened,
  one `section` per source module, with the auxiliary-lemma cache reset at each module
  boundary so `_proof_N` names match the per-module library build. Layout as in
  `catskillsresearch/scott_models`: the Challenge imports only Mathlib and states the compared
  theorems under the same fully-qualified names with `sorry` proofs. The definitions (and the
  lemmas those definitions use) are copied as written; every other theorem/lemma (and
  `**Subgoal**` helper def) not reachable by name from the compared statements or the copied
  definitions is commented out completely (`/- [omitted from the Challenge: …] … -/`), so it
  adds no declarations. Vendored code (`vendor/`, part of the submission) is compiled as
  lean_libs of this package (`srcDir = "vendor/<pkg>"` in `lakefile.toml`), never as Lake path
  dependencies, so a Comparator build writes only under `.lake/`; see `vendor/FROZEN.txt`.
  The generator adds a vendored import to the Challenge only if a kept module still needs it
  (currently none).
* `WeakPathwiseItoComparator/Solution.lean` imports the `WeakPathwiseIto` library, which supplies
  the real proofs (vendored `BrownianMotion` included).
* Checks: `bash scripts/compare_challenge_solution_types.sh` (types of compared names, plus
  the strict closure check `scripts/compare_challenge_solution_strict.sh`),
  `python3 scripts/check_module_name_clash.py`, and the full toolkit
  `bash scripts/palomar_preflight.sh --mechanical-only`.
* Blueprint stage: the library proofs are `sorry`, so Palomar mechanical verification
  (no `sorry` in Solution's closure) is expected to fail until the holes are closed.
